Read and write Lucid matrix keys

Source: R/lucid.R
readLucid.Rd

Lucid (Identic / Lucidcentral) is a widely used commercial program for interactive matrix keys: "entities" (taxa) scored for the states of "features" (characters). readLucid() reads a key exported from the Lucid Builder into a character matrix (see readSDD() for the convention) and writeLucid() writes a matrix in a form the Builder imports.

Usage

readLucid(
  file,
  format = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NA,
  entities = c("columns", "rows"),
  scores = c(1, 2, 3),
  fullNames = FALSE
)

writeLucid(
  x,
  file,
  format = c("csv", "sdd"),
  characters = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NULL,
  entities = c("columns", "rows"),
  title = NULL
)

Arguments

file

Path of the file to read or write.

format

"csv", "sdd" or (reading only) "lif3"; by default worked out from the file.

taxon

Name of the taxon column of the matrix.

sep

Separator between the states of a variable taxon in one cell.

inapplicable

For readers, the cell value to give "not applicable" (default NA, the same as unknown). For writers, the cell value that means "not applicable" (default NULL: none).

entities

For CSV: whether the entities (taxa) are the "columns" (Lucid's default) or the "rows" (its "transposed" export).

scores

Which Lucid scores mean that the taxon has the state.

fullNames

If TRUE, name characters and taxa by their whole path in Lucid's feature and entity trees ("Flowers:Petals:Colour") rather than by the last step ("Colour"). Names that would be ambiguous are always given in full.

x

A character matrix (data frame), or the list returned by readLucid(), readSDD(), readDELTA() or readXper().

characters

Optional data frame describing the characters (Character, Type, States, Unit); see writeSDD().

title

Title of the dataset (SDD only).

Value

readLucid() returns a tdwgData list like readSDD(): matrix, characters (Character, Type, States, Unit, Path), taxa (Taxon, Path) and meta. writeLucid() returns file, invisibly.

Formats

Lucid has several export formats, and they are not equally well documented:

  • "csv" (Lucid Builder: File > Export Key and Import Key, file type CSV). Documented in the Lucid Builder help, which also offers a small example key with its CSV export: the first row holds the entities, every further row one state named Feature:State (a colon-separated path through the feature tree), and the cells hold the scores 0 absent, 1 present, 2 rarely present, 3 uncertain, 4 present by misinterpretation, 5 rarely present by misinterpretation, 6 not scoped. A numeric feature is one row named Feature# with cells score type:rare low:low:high:rare high, or a plain 0 when it is not scored. This is the format writeLucid() writes by default, and the documented way to get a matrix into Lucid. Use entities = "rows" for the Builder's "transposed" variant.

  • "sdd": Lucid exports matrix keys as SDD, the TDWG standard; the file is read with readSDD() and written with writeSDD().

  • "lif3" (Lucid Interchange Format 3, .lif3): an XML file. Lucid publishes no schema or description of it beyond saying that it is XML, so readLucid() reads it as far as real exported files show how: features, states and entities (<item>), the feature and entity trees, and the multistate scores. This was checked against four published keys (Lucid 3 and Lucid 4 exports), one of which was also published as SDD: the two readings agree in all 3454 scores. Those files only use the scores 1 (present) and 3 (uncertain); the scores 2, 4, 5 and 6 are taken to mean what they mean in CSV, as they do in the Builder's own key files, which store scores in the same elements. No real LIF3 file with numeric scores was found: they are read when they are laid out as in the Builder's own key files (<scored_data> with omin, nmin, nmax, omax), and otherwise left out with a warning. Units, dependencies, text scores, subsets and media of a LIF3 file are not read (a warning says so when the file has dependencies or text scores), and dimoose does not write LIF3; export CSV or SDD from the Builder when you need those.

  • LIF (Lucid 2, .lif, a sectioned text file) and the Builder's "XML Dataset" are not publicly specified; readLucid() stops and asks for a CSV or SDD export instead of guessing.

Scores

By default a taxon gets a state when it is scored present (1), rarely present (2) or uncertain (3) for it; states scored only "by misinterpretation" are left out, because the taxon does not really have them. A feature for which every state of a taxon is uncertain, or nothing is scored, gives NA; "not scoped" gives inapplicable. writeLucid() writes 1 for every state in a cell and 0 otherwise, and 6 for cells equal to inapplicable.

For numeric features the Lucid help gives the layout of the cell but not the values its score type can take. The one real export at hand uses 1 for a scored range and a plain 0 for a feature that is not scored, and that is all writeLucid() writes: 1:rare low:low:high:rare high for a value or range, 0 for NA. A numeric cell equal to inapplicable is also written as 0, with a warning, because no score for "not scoped" is documented for numeric features. On reading, type 1 gives the range, 0 gives NA, 6 is taken as "not scoped" by analogy with the multistate scores, and any other type gives NA with a warning.

Text characters cannot be stored in a Lucid matrix and are left out with a warning. Colons in names are replaced, because Lucid reads them as steps of a path; data that was read from Lucid keeps its paths (the Path columns of characters and taxa). Units of numeric features are not part of the CSV format. No file written by dimoose has been imported into the Lucid Builder.

References

Lucid Builder help, "CSV (Comma Separated Value) Files" and "Importing and Exporting", https://help.lucidcentral.org/lucid/.

See also

readLucidKey() for Lucid pathway (dichotomous) keys, readSDD(), readDELTA().

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "bears-lucid.csv", package = "dimoose")
d <- readLucid(f)
d$matrix
#>                    Taxon      Colour Shoulder hump                Diet
#> 1           Ursus arctos       brown       present mixed/mostly plants
#> 2        Ursus maritimus       white        absent         mostly meat
#> 3       Ursus americanus brown/black        absent               mixed
#> 4 Ailuropoda melanoleuca white/black        absent       mostly plants
#>   Head and body length
#> 1    (1.4-)1.7-2.8(-3)
#> 2    (1.8-)2-2.5(-2.8)
#> 3        (1.2-)1.3-1.9
#> 4              1.2-1.9
d$characters
#>              Character        Type                          States Unit
#> 1               Colour categorical               white/brown/black     
#> 2        Shoulder hump categorical                  present/absent     
#> 3                 Diet categorical mostly meat/mixed/mostly plants     
#> 4 Head and body length        real                                     
#>                        Path
#> 1               Coat:Colour
#> 2             Shoulder hump
#> 3                      Diet
#> 4 Body:Head and body length

out <- writeLucid(d, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"))
readLines(out)
#>  [1] ",\"Ursidae:Ursus:Ursus arctos\",\"Ursidae:Ursus:Ursus maritimus\",\"Ursidae:Ursus:Ursus americanus\",\"Ursidae:Ailuropoda:Ailuropoda melanoleuca\""
#>  [2] "\"Coat:Colour:white\",0,1,0,1"                                                                                                                     
#>  [3] "\"Coat:Colour:brown\",1,0,1,0"                                                                                                                     
#>  [4] "\"Coat:Colour:black\",0,0,1,1"                                                                                                                     
#>  [5] "\"Shoulder hump:present\",1,0,0,0"                                                                                                                 
#>  [6] "\"Shoulder hump:absent\",0,1,1,1"                                                                                                                  
#>  [7] "\"Diet:mostly meat\",0,1,0,0"                                                                                                                      
#>  [8] "\"Diet:mixed\",1,0,1,0"                                                                                                                            
#>  [9] "\"Diet:mostly plants\",1,0,0,1"                                                                                                                    
#> [10] "\"Body:Head and body length#\",1:1.4:1.7:2.8:3,1:1.8:2:2.5:2.8,1:1.2:1.3:1.9:1.9,1:1.2:1.2:1.9:1.9"                                                
identical(readLucid(out)$matrix, d$matrix)
#> [1] TRUE
